prompt.zh-TW: 晨光印刷的股價 {{money:vars.priceA}}、每股盈餘 {{money:vars.epsA}}，本益比 {{number:vars.peA|unit=times}}；星河軟體的股價 {{money:vars.priceB}}、每股盈餘 {{money:vars.epsB}}，本益比 {{number:vars.peB|unit=times}}。兩家的每股盈餘一樣。下面哪一句解讀最合理？
prompt.en: Morning Light Printing: share price {{money:vars.priceA}}, earnings per share {{money:vars.epsA}}, P/E {{number:vars.peA|unit=times}}. Starriver Software: share price {{money:vars.priceB}}, earnings per share {{money:vars.epsB}}, P/E {{number:vars.peB|unit=times}}. Both have the same earnings per share. Which reading is the most reasonable?

text.zh-TW: 市場為星河軟體每一元盈餘付的價格比較高
text.en: The market pays more for each dollar of Starriver Software’s earnings

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。本益比是「價格」除以「盈餘」，同樣的盈餘配更高的價格，倍數就高；它說的是市場付了多少，不是公司賺了多少。倍數高通常反映市場對它未來成長比較樂觀，也可能只是股價偏貴。
feedback.en: That is right. The P/E ratio is price divided by earnings; the same earnings at a higher price give a higher multiple. It tells you what the market pays, not what the company earns. A high multiple usually reflects more optimistic growth expectations, or it may simply mean the share is dear.

text.zh-TW: 星河軟體比較賺錢，因為它的倍數比較高
text.en: Starriver Software is more profitable, because its multiple is higher

feedback.zh-TW: 你注意到倍數不同，這是對的起點。但兩家的每股盈餘一模一樣，差的是股價；倍數高是因為市場付得多，不是因為賺得多。
feedback.en: You noticed the multiples differ, which is the right start. But both companies have identical earnings per share; what differs is the price. The higher multiple comes from the market paying more, not from earning more.

text.zh-TW: 晨光印刷的倍數比較低，代表它比較便宜、值得買
text.en: Morning Light Printing has the lower multiple, so it is cheaper and worth buying

feedback.zh-TW: 倍數低確實表示每一元盈餘的價格較低，這部分沒錯。但「低」可能反映市場預期成長慢或風險高，便宜不等於值得買。
feedback.en: A lower multiple does mean a lower price per dollar of earnings, that much is right. But a low multiple may reflect slower expected growth or higher risk, and cheap does not mean worth buying.

explanation.zh-TW: {{option:o_d4p2}}抓到了本益比的本質：市場為每一元盈餘付出的價格。{{option:o_e5q1}}把價格差當成獲利差；{{option:o_f6r8}}把低倍數直接當成便宜又該買。本章是會計觀念練習，不是投資建議。
explanation.en: {{option:o_d4p2}} captures what the P/E ratio is: the price the market pays per dollar of earnings. {{option:o_e5q1}} mistakes a price difference for a profit difference; {{option:o_f6r8}} jumps from a low multiple to cheap and worth buying. This chapter is an accounting concept exercise, not investment advice.
